timeline.text: Patricia Hall reports bradycardia with renal failure and hyperkalemia. The nurse notes profound bradycardia with hypotension and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with hyperkalemia. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show ECG shows severe bradycardia with widened QRS. The cue pattern supports BRASH syndrome from AV nodal blocker accumulation and hyperkalemia.

Orders are initiated for place on cardiac monitor and notify provider and stabilize myocardium with calcium as ordered. The nurse avoids give additional beta blocker for hypertension because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, heart rate improves after hyperkalemia treatment. The nurse continues reassessment because creatinine remains elevated.
Final reassessment shows blood pressure improves. Ongoing concern remains because AV nodal blockers remain held pending review.

patient.name: Charles Morgan
patient.chief_concern: syncope with heart rate in the 30s
patient.past_medical_history: Relevant risk factors and comorbidities are disclosed progressively in the EHR.
patient.social_history: Support person or contact per chart.

chief_concern_card.value: syncope with heart rate in the 30s

timeline.text: Charles Morgan reports syncope with heart rate in the 30s. The nurse notes syncope with injury risk and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with heart rate 32 beats/min. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show ECG shows complete AV dissociation with ventricular escape rhythm. The cue pattern supports Complete heart block with poor perfusion.
Orders are initiated for place on defibrillator/pacing pads and notify provider/cardiology immediately. The nurse avoids give scheduled AV nodal blocker because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, perfusion improves after pacing. The nurse continues reassessment because temporary pacing still required.
Final reassessment shows dizziness resolves. Ongoing concern remains because permanent pacemaker evaluation pending.

timeline.text: Noelle Martin reports thunderclap headache and neck stiffness. The nurse notes worst headache of life and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with neck stiffness and photophobia. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show Head CT shows diffuse subarachnoid hemorrhage in basal cisterns. The cue pattern supports Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage with rebleeding and vasospasm risk.
Orders are initiated for maintain neurologic monitoring and BP goals and administer nimodipine as ordered. The nurse avoids give aspirin for headache because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, headache decreases after analgesia. The nurse continues reassessment because vasospasm window remains ahead.
Final reassessment shows aneurysm coiling completed. Ongoing concern remains because sodium remains low.

timeline.text: Leo Anderson reports inferior MI with hypotension and clear lungs. The nurse notes inferior ST elevation with right-sided lead changes and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with hypotension with clear lung sounds. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show ECG shows inferior STEMI with ST elevation in right-sided lead V4R. The cue pattern supports Right ventricular myocardial infarction with preload-dependent hypotension.

Orders are initiated for avoid nitrates if RV infarct/hypotension suspected and maintain IV access and cautious fluids as ordered. The nurse avoids give nitrates for all chest pain because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, BP improves after cautious fluid and reperfusion plan. The nurse continues reassessment because bradyarrhythmia watch continues.
Final reassessment shows chest pain decreases. Ongoing concern remains because reperfusion completion still required.

timeline.text: Marcus Evans reports confusion with thrombocytopenia and hemolysis. The nurse notes new confusion and headache and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with platelets extremely low. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show Peripheral smear shows schistocytes consistent with microangiopathic hemolysis. The cue pattern supports TTP with microangiopathic hemolysis and neurologic involvement.

Final reassessment shows mental status improves. Ongoing concern remains because renal function still abnormal.

timeline.text: Ethan Moore reports toxic child with stridor and thick secretions. The nurse notes high fever with toxic appearance and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with stridor and severe cough. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show Neck imaging suggests subglottic narrowing; bronchoscopy shows purulent tracheal membranes. The cue pattern supports Bacterial tracheitis with impending airway obstruction.
Orders are initiated for call airway/ENT/anesthesia team early and prepare controlled airway management. The nurse avoids perform aggressive throat exam alone because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, airway secured safely. The nurse continues reassessment because secretions remain thick.
Final reassessment shows SpO2 improves after airway support. Ongoing concern remains because IV antibiotics continue.

chief_concern_card.value: drooling after suspected button battery ingestion

timeline.text: Ava Robinson reports drooling after suspected button battery ingestion. The nurse notes missing button battery from remote and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with drooling and refusal to swallow. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show Chest/neck x-ray shows double-rim button battery lodged in upper esophagus. The cue pattern supports Button battery lodged in esophagus with caustic injury risk.
Orders are initiated for keep NPO and notify GI/ENT/surgery emergently. The nurse avoids wait for battery to pass in stool because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, battery removed endoscopically. The nurse continues reassessment because esophageal injury monitoring remains.
Final reassessment shows drooling decreases. Ongoing concern remains because delayed fistula risk education needed.

timeline.text: Grace Williams reports fever and flank pain at 24 weeks gestation. The nurse notes fever with costovertebral-angle tenderness and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with tachycardia and hypotension. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria; fetal monitoring shows uterine irritability. The cue pattern supports Pyelonephritis in pregnancy with sepsis and preterm labor risk.
Orders are initiated for admit for IV antibiotics and fluids as ordered and monitor maternal sepsis indicators. The nurse avoids send home with oral fluids only because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, temperature decreases after antibiotics. The nurse continues reassessment because uterine irritability persists.
Final reassessment shows maternal BP stabilizes. Ongoing concern remains because culture-directed therapy pending.
